titlePlain: Azure Firewall and AWS Network Firewall
subtitle: Lesson 14 · Network Security Across Both Clouds

code:
RuleCollectionGroup: "DefaultNetworkRuleCollectionGroup"
  RuleCollection: "Allow-DNS" (priority 100)
    Rule: Allow UDP 53 from 10.0.0.0/16 to 168.63.129.16
  RuleCollection: "Allow-Microsoft-Update" (priority 200, Application)
    Rule: Allow https to *.windowsupdate.com from 10.0.0.0/16
caption: Network rules filter by IP/port; application rules filter by FQDN — something an NSG can't do.

eyebrow: AWS Network Firewall — stateful Suricata rule
code:
alert tls $HOME_NET any -> $EXTERNAL_NET any \
  (tls.sni; content:"update.microsoft.com"; nocase; \
   msg:"allowed update domain"; sid:1000001; rev:1)
caption: FQDN filtering in AWS Network Firewall is a Suricata rule, not a separate rule type.

code:
Azure Firewall:
  Standard  -> network + application + NAT rules, threat intel
  Premium   -> + TLS inspection, IDPS, URL filtering

AWS Network Firewall:
  Stateless rule groups -> fast 5-tuple pass (pass/drop/forward_to_sfe)
  Stateful rule groups   -> Suricata engine, always available
caption: AWS bundles deep inspection into the stateful engine; Azure gates it behind the Premium SKU.
